title: CASP schedule file
description: casp/schedule.json — an OPT-IN declaration of dated claims about a project's phases. A cockpit that never scaffolds this file sees no CASP-SCHEDULE-* rule at all. CASP verifies a recorded schedule against the phase lists and the calendar — that it does not contradict itself, that it dates phases that exist, and that a queued phase has not silently slipped into the past. It never proposes a date, never estimates, and never fails a push because of the clock. See docs/rules.md and docs/what-casp-proves.md.

schema_version.description: The schedule.json schema version. Additive fields do not bump it.

anchors.description: Fixed dates the project is organised around (a freeze, a launch). ORDERED: an anchor's position in this array IS the declared chronology, which is why CASP-SCHEDULE-003 fails on an array whose dates are not strictly ascending. There is deliberately no `order` field — a second declaration of the same thing is one more thing that can contradict itself.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the file, referenced by a due entry's `before`.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD only — no time, no zone, no relative expression. A zone makes the same file resolve differently on two machines, which is the determinism bug in miniature.

note.description: Tolerated and IGNORED. Nothing in casp parses it; parsing free text would require a model.

due.description: A date attached to a phase. The join key is the PHASE NAME — the unit phases_shipped / phases_queued / phases_backlog already verify — not the prompt path, which is one indirection away and renames more often.

phase.description: A phase name. Absent from all three phase lists → CASP-SCHEDULE-002 (WARN, not FAIL: phases get renamed mid-flight, and failing the push for a rename teaches operators to delete the schedule).

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD only. In the past while the phase is still queued or backlog → CASP-SCHEDULE-004 (WARN, always; the clock never changes the exit code).

before.description: The id of a declared anchor this phase must land strictly before. An unknown id is a schema failure (CASP-SCHEDULE-001); a queued phase dated on or after its anchor is CASP-SCHEDULE-003 (FAIL — the file contradicts itself, no clock involved).

note.description: Tolerated and IGNORED, exactly as on an anchor.
